definitions: Edward Lee Thorndike (1874-1949), an American psychologist who spent nearly his entire career at Teachers College, Columbia University. His work on comparative psychology and the learning process led to the theory of connectionism and helped lay the scientific foundation for educational psychology.
examples: Thorndike's law of effect is a fundamental principle in behaviorism.
The Thorndike family has a long history in New England.
Many students study Thorndike's contributions to psychology.
